question: What is the main benefit of eating by mouth compared to other feeding methods?

options.A: It guarantees maximum daily weight gain
options.B: It completely eliminates the risk of infection
options.C: It stops all digestive secretions immediately

explanation: Using the natural digestive tract keeps the gut working normally and maintains mucosal health better than artificial routes. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why should you encourage a patient to feed themselves as much as possible?

options.A: To completely remove the need for nursing staff supervision
options.B: To prevent the client from ever needing nutritional supplements
options.C: To promote client independence and preserve dignity
options.D: To ensure the meal tray is finished within ten minutes

explanation: Allowing clients to do what they can for themselves boosts their self-esteem and maintains their functional abilities. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h1)

question: What clinical sign must a patient show before you attempt to feed them by mouth?

options.A: A completely empty stomach for six hours
options.D: An active bowel sound in all quadrants

explanation: A client must be awake and alert to safely manage food in the mouth and swallow without choking. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h2)

question: A patient with a history of stroke is coughing slightly and breathing fast when you arrive with lunch. What should you do first?

options.A: Encourage them to lie flat in bed while eating
options.B: Feed them very small bites of soft food quickly
options.C: Mix all their food and liquids together in a cup
options.D: Delay feeding and assess their respiratory status

explanation: Rapid breathing and coughing indicate a high risk for aspiration, meaning feeding must be postponed until they stabilize. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h2)

question: What is the ideal bed angle for feeding a patient who must remain in bed?
explanation: A high Fowler's position between 75 and 90 degrees uses gravity to help send food down the esophagus safely. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h3)

question: Why is the chin-tuck maneuver useful when a patient is swallowing?

options.A: It protects the airway by narrowing the larynx entrance
options.B: It opens the nasal passages to improve oxygen intake
options.C: It speeds up digestion in the stomach
options.D: It stretches the jaw muscles to increase bite strength

explanation: Tucking the chin closes off the windpipe entrance, lowering the chance that food will slip into the lungs. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h3)

question: Where should you place food in the mouth if a patient has weakness on one side of their face?

options.A: On the weaker side of the mouth
options.B: On the stronger side of the mouth
options.C: Directly in the center of the tongue
options.D: Against the roof of the mouth

explanation: Placing food on the unaffected side helps the client chew and move the food more effectively. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h4)

question: Which of these practices should you avoid when assisting a patient with meals?

options.A: Checking the diet ticket before starting
options.B: Offering small sips of water between bites
options.C: Describing the different foods on the plate
options.D: Rushing the client to finish the tray quickly

explanation: Rushing increases the risk of choking and takes away the social pleasure of eating. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h4)

question: What is a common sign that a patient may be experiencing mild or silent aspiration?

options.A: Swelling in the hands and feet
options.B: A wet or gurgling voice after swallowing
options.C: Redness of the skin around the nose
options.D: A sudden increase in overall body temperature

explanation: A wet-sounding voice often means liquid or food residue is sitting near the vocal cords and airway. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why should a patient remain upright for 30 minutes after finishing a meal?

options.A: To prevent food from returning through reflux
options.B: To help them fall asleep faster after eating
options.C: To make it easier to clear the bedside table
options.D: To allow their blood pressure to normalize

explanation: Gravity helps keep stomach contents down, reducing the chance of regurgitation and secondary aspiration. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the best way to record how much of a meal a patient ate?

options.A: Weighing the food tray before and after
options.B: Estimating the percentage or fraction consumed
options.C: Asking family members to guess the volume
options.D: Counting every single grain of rice left

explanation: Charting approximate amounts like one-half or 50% gives healthcare team members a clear picture of nutritional intake. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h6)

question: You notice food debris trapped inside a patient's cheek after they finish eating. What should you do?

options.A: Gently clean the mouth and check for pocketed food
options.B: Leave it alone until the next scheduled dental visit
options.C: Give the client a large heavy meal to push it down
options.D: Turn the client flat on their side immediately

explanation: Pocketed food can easily slide into the airway later, so clearing the mouth is essential after every meal. [learn more](BMP110_U5_T7#BMP110_U5_T7_h6)
